   340	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- renderers

   346	  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;

   348	'

   350	render_register() {
   351	    jq -r "$JQ_DEFS"'
   352	      .guards as $g
   353	      | "# Guard register",
   354	        "",
   355	        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh from .claude/settings.json, the fence and validator markers and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml. Do not edit by hand: edit the origin map and regenerate (.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table); CI runs --check. -->",
   356	        "",
   357	        "Every guard Loa ships, with its class, status, origin, knob and floor flag. Structural only: the 30-day yield of a host is untracked, in `.run/guard-yield.md` and `.run/guard-yield.json` (regenerate with `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`). Classes: harness (the model cannot override it), script (a script checks or reports), prose (the model is asked to comply). Status: dormant means armed only by the env var in the knob column; telemetry means it observes and never refuses.",
   358	        "",
   359	        "- guards: \($g | length)",
   360	        "- guards_without_origin: \($g | map(select((.origin.ref // "") == "")) | length)",
   361	        "- dormant: \($g | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length)",
   362	        "- floor: \($g | map(select(.floor == true)) | length)",
   363	        (kinds[] as $k | ($g | map(select(.kind == $k))) as $rows | select($rows | length > 0)
   364	          | "",
   365	            "## \($k) (\($rows | length))",
   366	            "",
   367	            "| id | class | status | origin | knob | floor | registrations |",
   368	            "|----|-------|--------|--------|------|-------|---------------|",
   369	            ($rows[] | "| \(.id | cell) | \(.class | cell) | \(.status | cell) | \(origin_txt | cell) | \(.knob | cell) | \(.floor | yesno) | \(regs) |"))
   370	    ' <<<"$MAP_JSON"

   373	render_hooks_block() {

   376	      | "<!-- guard-register:begin -->",
   377	        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table from .claude/settings.json and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml; do not edit by hand. Full register: grimoires/loa/guards.md -->",

   379	        "|-------|---------|--------|--------|------|---------|",
   380	        ($hooks[] | . as $h | $by[$h.id] as $r
   381	          | "| \($h.event | cell) | \(if $h.matcher == "" then "(all)" else ($h.matcher | cell) end) | `\(if $h.wrapped then "hook-guard.sh " else "" end)\($h.id | ltrimstr("hook:") | cell)` | \($r.status | cell) | \($r.knob | cell) | \($r.note // "" | cell) |"),

   386	# Rewrites the marker block of $HOOKS_REF into $2 (exit 3 when the markers are absent or repeated).

   465	# Heredoc classification: the FR-6 classifier when present (heredoc_nonexec <command>

tests/fixtures/*.pem
tests/fixtures/*.key

# Ephemeral signed license fixtures (#953 batch-1).
# Regenerated by tests/fixtures/ensure_license_fixtures.sh on first test run.
# They're paired with the gitignored mock_public_key.pem; committing them
# would create constant drift on every test run.
tests/fixtures/*_license.json

# Dependencies
node_modules/
.pnp
.pnp.js

# Testing
coverage/
*.log

# Production builds
build/
dist/
out/

# Bridgebuilder ships its compiled dist to submodule consumers
# (#607: multi-model-pipeline.js and other newer modules were getting
# silently ignored by the `dist/` pattern above, causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
# when the skill runs from a submodule consumer). The skill's dist/ IS
# shipping infrastructure — un-ignore it explicitly.
!.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/
!.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/**
!evals/fixtures/review-prs/*/*/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/
!evals/fixtures/review-prs/*/*/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/**

# Environment variables
.env
.env.local
.env.development.local
.env.test.local
.env.production.local

# IDE and Editor
.vscode/
.idea/

# Claude Code config (local workspace settings, prompts, scratchpad)
.claude/config/

# GPT review context (dynamically generated based on config)
.claude/context/gpt-review-active.md

# Local settings overrides (user-specific feedback trace configuration)
# Contains opt-in trace collection settings - never commit to repository
.claude/settings.local.json
*.swp
*.swo
*~
.DS_Store

# OS

     1	# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
     2	#
     3	# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
     4	# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
     5	#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
     6	#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
     7	#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
     8	#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
     9	#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
    10	# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
    11	# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
    12	schema_version: 1
    13	
    14	floor_guards:
    15	  - fence:FR-1.2b
    16	  - fence:FR-SZ
    17	  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
    18	  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
    19	  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
    20	  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
    21	  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP
    22	  - fence:FR-SZ-LINK
    23	  - fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
    24	  - fence:FR-SZ-TEE
    25	  - fence:FR-SZ2
    26	  - fence:FR-SZ2-COPY
    27	  - fence:FR-SZ2-INPLACE
    28	  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
    29	  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
    30	  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
    31	  - gate:verdict-derive
    32	  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
    33	  - policy:permission-deny-list
    34	  - policy:verdict-one-way-rule
    35	  - policy:operator-only-commands
    36	
    37	floor_keys:
    38	  - flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
    39	  - flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled
    40	  - "flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice"
    41	  - "destructive_command_guard.*"
    42	  - "implement_gate.*"
    43	  - hounfour.locality
    44	
    45	# Paths whose bytes must not change relative to origin/main during a cycle.
    46	floor_files:
    47	  - .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
    48	  - .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
    49	  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json
    50	  - .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt
    51	
    52	# Fence-corpus rows (by their `rule` field) that must not change relative to
    53	# origin/main. A trailing `*` is a prefix match.
    54	floor_corpus:
    55	  file: tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl
    56	  rules:
    57	    - FR-1.2b
    58	    - "FR-SZ*"

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`

     5	# SDD D-1.3, D-1.4)
     6	# guard-yield.sh over a fixture audit log and a rotated segment, at a fixed
     7	# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the
     8	# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
     9	# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
    10	# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
    11	# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    18	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    19	  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
    21	  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
    22	  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
    23	  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
    24	  export TMPDIR="$T"

    26	  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"
    27	  A="$T/audit.jsonl"
    28	  row() {  # ts pattern cwd command [extra-json]
    29	    jq -cn --arg ts "$1" --arg p "$2" --arg cwd "$3" --arg c "$4" --argjson x "${5:-{\}}" \
    30	      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
    31	  }
    32	  {
    33	    # live, inside the repo
    34	    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"            # heredoc → likely FP
    35	    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
    36	    row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP
    37	    row "2026-10-13T23:59:00Z" "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS" "$ROOT" "cd sub && rm -rf ./.cache"             # prose class WITH verb → real
    38	    # replays
    39	    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
    40	    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
    41	    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
    42	    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
    43	      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"
    44	    done
    45	    # outside the window
    46	    row "2026-08-01T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~9"
    47	    # implement-gate telemetry and ask
    48	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:00:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "telemetry", cwd: "x"}'
    49	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:05:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", cwd: "x"}'
    50	    # a non-block row and an unparseable line
    51	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:10:00Z", tool: "Bash", command: "ls", cwd: "x"}'
    52	    printf 'this is not json\n'
    53	  } > "$A"
    54	  # the rotated segment holds the one real P3 catch
    55	  row "2026-10-10T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~3" > "$A.1"

    57	}

   129	BATCH_DIR="$SUITE_DIR/$BATCH"

   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

   140	bad = []

   142	    if not line.strip():

   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)

   171	  cli_version="$("$claude_bin" --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo unknown)"

   173	  harness_commit="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
   174	  [[ -n "$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" status --porcelain -- evals/harness evals/graders evals/suites evals/tasks 2>/dev/null)" ]] && harness_dirty=true

   179	    --arg suite "$SUITE" --arg batch "$BATCH" \
   180	    --arg source_commit "$SRC_FULL" --arg source_worktree "$WORKTREE" \
   181	    --arg harness_commit "$harness_commit" --argjson harness_dirty "$harness_dirty" \
   182	    --arg model_id "$MODEL" --arg cli "$claude_bin" --arg cli_version "$cli_version" \
   183	    --argjson trials "$TRIALS" --argjson concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --argjson retry_wait "$RETRY_WAIT" \
   184	    --argjson per_trial "$per_trial" --arg max_turns "${EVAL_MAX_TURNS:-40}" \

   186	    --argjson planned "${#PLAN[@]}" --arg digest "$CORPUS_DIGEST" \
   187	    --arg os "$(uname -srm)" --arg bash_v "$BASH_VERSION" \
   188	    --arg jq_v "$(jq --version 2>/dev/null)" --arg yq_v "$(yq --version 2>/dev/null)" \
   189	    --arg py_v "$(python3 --version 2>/dev/null)" --arg git_v "$(git --version 2>/dev/null)" \
   190	    --arg created "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --argjson dry "$dry" \
   191	    --arg suite_file "evals/suites/$SUITE.yaml" \
   192	    '{schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, batch: $batch, dry_run: $dry, created: $created,
   193	      source_commit: $source_commit, source_worktree: $source_worktree,
   194	      harness_commit: $harness_commit, harness_dirty: $harness_dirty, suite_file: $suite_file,
   195	      model_id: $model_id,
   196	      executor: {cli: $cli, cli_version: $cli_version, tools: "Read,Grep,Glob,Write", restricted: true,
   197	                 permission_mode: "acceptEdits", max_turns: ($max_turns | tonumber), effort: "task/skill default",
   198	                 timeout_per_trial_s: $per_trial, concurrency: $concurrency, retry: {transport_retries: 1, wait_s: $retry_wait},
   199	                 subagent_model: "pinned to model_id (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL); parent-session coupling unset",
   200	                 seed: null},
   201	      arms: $arms, fixtures: $fixtures, trials: $trials, trials_planned: $planned,
   202	      corpus: {manifest: "evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS", sha256: $digest,
   203	               verified: "every entry before the batch; the fixture'"'"'s entries before each trial"},
   204	      environment: {os: $os, bash: $bash_v, jq: $jq_v, yq: $yq_v, python: $py_v, git: $git_v}}' > "$out.tmp"
   205	  mv "$out.tmp" "$out"
   206	}
   207	
   208	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
   209	  mpath="$BATCH_DIR/MANIFEST.json"
   210	  [[ -f "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json" ]] && mpath="$BATCH_DIR/MANIFEST.dry-run.json"
   211	  write_manifest "$mpath" true
   212	  echo "run-arms (dry run): suite=$SUITE batch=$BATCH source=$SRC12 model=$MODEL worktree=$WORKTREE"
   213	  echo "planned trials: ${#PLAN[@]} (${#FIXTURES[@]} fixtures x ${#ARMS[@]} arms x $TRIALS trials, concurrency $CONCURRENCY)"
   214	  i=0
   215	  for p in "${PLAN[@]}"; do
   216	    i=$((i + 1)); IFS='|' read -r a f t <<<"$p"
   217	    printf '%4d  %-16s %-6s trial %s  task %s-%s\n' "$i" "$a" "$f" "$t" "$TASK_PREFIX" "$f"
   218	  done
   219	  echo "manifest: $mpath"
   220	  exit 0
   221	fi
   222	
   223	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
   224	command -v "$CLAUDE_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -x "$CLAUDE_BIN" ]] || die "executor CLI not found: $CLAUDE_BIN"
   225

   227	mkdir -p "$CACHE_ROOT"
   228	if [[ -e "$WORKTREE" ]]; then
   229	  [[ "$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" == "$SRC_FULL" ]] \
   230	    || die "$WORKTREE exists but is not at $SRC_FULL; remove it with git worktree remove"

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries

   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"

   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)

   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())

  - "**/*.bats"

# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):

```bash
worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

## Origin

- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).

## Related rules

- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.
- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` framework boundary (Bash writes now fenced by FR-SZ2).

    48	    done < <(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")
    49	}
    50

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
     4	# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
     5	# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
     9	#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
    10	#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
    11	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
    12	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
    13	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
    14	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
    15	#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
    16	#
    17	# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
    18	# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
    19	#
    20	# Writes (seed):
    21	#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
    22	#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
    23	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
    24	#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
    25	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
    26	#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
    27	#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
    28	#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
    29	#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
    30	#
    31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
    32	# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
    33	# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
    34	#

    36	# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
    37	# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
    38	# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
    39	# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
    40	# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
    41	# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
    42	# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
    43	# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
    44	# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
    45	# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
    46	# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
    47	#
    48	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
    49	# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
    50	# =============================================================================

    52	export LC_ALL=C
    53	
    54	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

    65	ap.add_argument("record_ref", nargs="?")
    66	ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--base"); ap.add_argument("--head"); ap.add_argument("--fix")
    67	ap.add_argument("--feedback"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    68	ap.add_argument("--build-manifest", metavar="FIXTURE"); ap.add_argument("--approve", metavar="FIXTURE")
    69	ap.add_argument("--by"); ap.add_argument("--freeze", action="store_true"); ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    70	ap.add_argument("--repo", default=HARNESS_ROOT)
    71	ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "fixtures", "review-prs"))

    80	LABELS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "labels")
    81	MANIFESTS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "manifests")
    82	FX_RX = re.compile(r"^pr-[0-9]{2}$")
    83	HEADER = ["defect_id", "severity", "category", "file", "must_match", "label_source", "source"]
    84	
    85	def fail(msg, code=1):
    86	    print(f"seed-corpus: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    87	    sys.exit(code)
    88	
    89	def git(*a, binary=False, check=True):
    90	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True, text=not binary)
    91	    if check and p.returncode != 0:
    92	        fail(f"git {' '.join(a[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr if not binary else p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')).strip()[:300]}")

    94	
    95	def rev(r):
    96	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{r}^{{commit}}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    97	    if p.returncode != 0:
    98	        fail(f"missing commit: {r}")
    99	    return p.stdout.strip()

   103	    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else None
   104	
   105	CTRL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f  ]")

   107	    s = CTRL.sub(" ", s)
   108	    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
   109	    return s if len(s) <= cap else s[: cap - 1].rstrip() + "…"
   110	
   111	SECRET_RX = [re.compile(p) for p in (
   112	    r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", r"sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}", r"ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}", r"gho_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}",
   113	    r"glpat-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}", r"xox[bpors]-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+", r"sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}",
   114	    r"password\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}", r"secret\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}")]
   115	def has_secret(s):
   116	    return any(r.search(s) for r in SECRET_RX)
   117	
   118	REDACTED = [0]
   119	def redact(b, count=True):
   120	    """Secret-shaped strings in verbatim copies of tracked files (fake test keys)
   121	    become a fixed marker, identically in base/, head/ and head.diff; line
   122	    numbers never move. Counted in the dropped report."""
   123	    if b is None:
   124	        return None
   125	    t = b.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(b, bytes) else b
   126	    for r in SECRET_RX:
   127	        t, n = r.subn("REDACTED-TEST-SECRET", t)
   128	        REDACTED[0] += n if count else 0
   129	    return t.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(b, bytes) else t
   130	
   131	def sha(path):
   132	    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
   133	
   134	def freeze():
   135	    entries = []
   136	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
   137	        for f in files:
   138	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
   139	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS":
   140	                entries.append(rel)
   141	    lines = [f"{sha(os.path.join(CORPUS, rel))}  {rel}" for rel in sorted(entries)]
   142	    open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
   143	    return len(lines)
   144	
   145	def check():
   146	    bad, n = [], 0
   147	    for line in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8"):
   148	        if not line.strip():
   149	            continue
   150	        n += 1
   151	        d, rel = line.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)
   152	        p = os.path.join(CORPUS, rel)
   153	        if not os.path.isfile(p) or sha(p) != d:
   154	            bad.append(rel)
   155	    listed = {l.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)[1] for l in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}
   156	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
   157	        for f in files:
   158	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
   159	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS" and rel not in listed:
   160	                bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
   161	    if bad:
   162	        fail("SHA256SUMS mismatch: " + ", ".join(bad[:20]))
   163	    print(f"corpus OK: {n} files match SHA256SUMS")
   164	
   165	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- labels I/O
   166	def read_labels(fx):
   167	    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
   168	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
   169	        fail(f"labels not found: {path}")
   170	    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
   171	    if not text or not re.match(r"^# approved-by: \S", text[0]):
   172	        fail(f"{path}: the first line must be '# approved-by: <who> <date>' (or 'pending')")
   173	    approved_by = text[0][len("# approved-by: "):].strip()
   174	    body = [l for l in text[1:] if l and not l.startswith("#")]
   175	    if not body or body[0].split("\t") != HEADER:
   176	        fail(f"{path}: header must be: " + "\t".join(HEADER))
   177	    rows = []
   178	    for i, l in enumerate(body[1:], 2):
   179	        cells = l.split("\t")
   180	        if len(cells) != len(HEADER):
   181	            fail(f"{path}: row {i} has {len(cells)} columns, want {len(HEADER)}")
   182	        rows.append(dict(zip(HEADER, cells)))
   183	    return approved_by, rows, text
   184	
   185	def unique_line(lines, needle):
   186	    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1) if needle in l]
   187	    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
   188	
   189	def build_manifest(fx):
   190	    approved_by, rows, _ = read_labels(fx)
   191	    fyaml = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "fixture.yaml")
   192	    meta = {}
   193	    for l in open(fyaml, encoding="utf-8"):
   194	        m = re.match(r"^(sprint|head_commit|fix_commit|record_ref):\s*\"?([^\"\n]*)\"?$", l)
   195	        if m:
   196	            meta[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
   197	    defects, regions, errors, order = {}, [], [], []
   198	    for r in rows:
   199	        if r["label_source"] not in ("review", "audit", "bridgebuilder", "fix"):
   200	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: label_source {r['label_source']!r}"); continue
   201	        hp = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "head", r["file"])
   202	        if not os.path.isfile(hp):
   203	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: head/{r['file']} missing"); continue
   204	        lines = open(hp, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
   205	        if r["label_source"] == "fix":
   206	            m = re.match(r"^fix/[0-9a-f]+:(\d+)-(\d+)$", r["source"])
   207	            if not m:
   208	                errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: fix source must be fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>"); continue
   209	            regions.append({"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "start": int(m.group(1)), "end": int(m.group(2)),
   210	                            "source": r["source"]})
   211	            continue
   212	        at = unique_line(lines, r["must_match"])
   213	        if at is None:
   214	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: must_match {r['must_match']!r} is not on exactly one line of head/{r['file']}"); continue
   215	        d = defects.get(r["defect_id"])
   216	        if d is None:
   217	            order.append(r["defect_id"])
   218	            defects[r["defect_id"]] = {"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "anchor_line": at, "anchors": [at],
   219	                                       "must_match": r["must_match"], "severity": r["severity"], "category": r["category"],
   220	                                       "label_source": r["label_source"], "source": r["source"],
   221	                                       "source_commit": meta.get("head_commit", "")[:8], "synthetic": False}
   222	        else:
   223	            if d["file"] != r["file"]:
   224	                errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: extra anchor rows must name the same file"); continue
   225	            d["anchors"].append(at)
   226	    if errors:
   227	        fail(f"{fx}: " + "; ".join(errors))

   229	    for k in order:
   230	        d = defects[k]
   231	        d["anchors"] = sorted(set(d["anchors"]))
   232	        if len(d["anchors"]) == 1:
   233	            del d["anchors"]
   234	        out.append(d)
   235	    man = {"fixture": fx, "approved": approved_by != "pending", "approved_by": approved_by,
   236	           "record": {"sprint": meta.get("sprint"), "record_ref": meta.get("record_ref"),
   237	                      "head_commit": meta.get("head_commit"), "fix_commit": meta.get("fix_commit")},
   238	           "defects": out, "fix_regions": regions}

   241	    return man

   243	# ------------------------------------------------------------ simple modes
   244	if args.check:
   245	    check(); sys.exit(0)
   246	if args.freeze:
   247	    print(f"froze {freeze()} files in SHA256SUMS"); sys.exit(0)
   248	if args.build_manifest:

   254	    sys.exit(0)

   259	    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
   260	    _, _, text = read_labels(fx)

  SUITE="all"

}

   corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS
 
+  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
+  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
+  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
+  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
+  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
+  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
+  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
+  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
+  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
+  #                can never license removing the control
+  arms:
+    - id: baseline
+      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
+      toggles: {}
+    - id: no_companion
+      description: >-
+        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
+        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
+        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
+      informational: true
+      toggles:
+        companion_voice: false
+    - id: no_karpathy
+      description: >-
+        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
+        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
+        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
+        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
+      toggles:
+        karpathy_block: false
+    - id: no_rule_files
+      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
+      toggles:
+        rule_files: false
+
+  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
+  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
+  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
+  threshold:
+    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
+    trials_required: 3
+    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
+    coverage_required: full
+    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
+    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
+    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
+    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
+    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
+    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
+    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
+    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
+    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
+    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
+    bootstrap:
+      method: percentile
+      level: 0.90
+      resample: fixtures
+      iterations: 2000
+
 ci:
   gate_type: advisory
   min_trials: 3

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)
    47	
    48	
    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows
    62	
    63

# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

 `compare.sh` refuses a baseline whose `prompt_tree_sha` equals the tree under comparison, whose
 `captured_at_commit` is not a descendant of the suite's `ab.floor_commit`, or whose `corpus_sha256`
 drifted (`evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats`). Tests: `evals/tests/{execute-agent,eval-recall-grader,implement-discipline-grader,recall-baseline-freshness}.bats`.
+
+## Control arms and the record corpus (cycle-129 FR-2)
+
+Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
+(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
+in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
+materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle
+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.
+
+The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
+branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
+live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
+explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
+re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
+only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
+`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.
+
+```bash
+# one suite, one batch, against a detached worktree pinned at the source commit
+./evals/harness/run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files \
+  --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,pr-03,pr-04,pr-05,pr-06,pr-07,pr-08 --trials 3 --source-commit 864069f2 --dry-run
+./evals/harness/report.sh --arms            # refuses until STATUS.json is complete; --partial for interim
+./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/baseline \
+  --arm-b evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/no_karpathy --metric recall
+```
+
+Tests: `evals/tests/{arm-toggles,run-arms,arms-report,seed-corpus}.bats`.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
#
# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
  mkdir -p "$B"
  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
  status_file complete
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

status_file() {  # status_file <state>
  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
}

# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
row() {
  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
}

full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
  local fx t
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
}

@test "AR-1 complete run: equal recall reads no recall loss, a large drop reads recall loss, the informational arm says so" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  full_arm no_rule_files 1
  full_arm no_karpathy 0.3333 "L2,L3" 1
  full_arm no_companion 1
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --date 2026-10-14
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*'
  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
  grep -E '^\| `no_companion` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q 'informational: yield only'
  grep -E '^\| `baseline` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '(reference)'
  # the interval of the drop and the missed labels are printed
  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\[0.667, 0.667\]'
  grep -q 'no_karpathy`: pr-01:L2 (3/3)' "$T/r.md"
  grep -q '^# Control-arm report — 2026-10-14' "$T/r.md"
  ! grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-2 a refuted-share rise beyond the threshold is a recall loss even with equal recall" {
  full_arm baseline 1 "" 0
  full_arm no_rule_files 1 "" 3
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
  grep -q 'refuted share 0.750 > baseline 0.000' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-3 a missing trial or fixture is inconclusive; model or source skew is inconclusive" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_rule_files "$fx" "$t" 1 ""; done; done
  row no_rule_files pr-03 1 1 ""
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_karpathy "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-opus-5-5; done; done
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_companion "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-fable-5-1 ffd25258; done; done
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
  grep -q 'coverage: pr-03 1/3' "$T/r.md"
  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
  grep -q 'source skew' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-4 a rule violation within the baseline's own trial-to-trial spread names no change (inconclusive)" {
  # baseline trial means 1.0, 0.6, 1.0 (spread 0.4); the arm sits 0.2 lower on every fixture
  local fx
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row baseline "$fx" 1 1 ""; row baseline "$fx" 2 0.6 ""; row baseline "$fx" 3 1 ""; done
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row no_rule_files "$fx" 1 0.8 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 2 0.4 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 3 0.8 ""; done
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
  grep -q 'no change can be named' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-5 STATUS.json not complete: refused (exit 1); --partial writes, says so, and every verdict is inconclusive" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  full_arm no_rule_files 1
  status_file running
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
  grep -q "not 'complete'" <<<"$output"
  [ ! -e "$T/r.md" ]
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --partial
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
  ! grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-7 a safeguard-refusal fallback to another model is skew: the arm is inconclusive and the fallback is named" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  full_arm no_rule_files 1
  # one no_rule_files trial moved to Opus on a refusal (models_used + refusal_fallbacks, as execute-agent records them)
  jq -c 'if .trial == 1 and .fixture == "pr-01" then .executor.models_used = {"claude-fable-5-1": 10, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 90}
         | .executor.refusal_fallbacks = [{"from":"claude-fable-5-1","to":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5","category":"cyber"}] else . end' \
    "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl" > "$B/x" && mv "$B/x" "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl"
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'

# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/loa-status-guards.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD D-1.5)
# `/loa` prints one Guards line: register counts from grimoires/loa/guards.md and
# the 30-day host yield from .run/guard-yield.json (never recomputed at status
# time), or the regenerate hint when the yield file is missing. Fixture files via

# =============================================================================

setup() {
  umask 022

  PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
  STATUS="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh"

7:**Beads**: The local-first task tracker, driven through its br command, that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
10:**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
12:**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
14:**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
16:**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
18:**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
21:**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
24:**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
26:**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
28:**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
30:**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
32:**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
35:**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
38:**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
40:**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
42:**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
44:**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
46:**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
48:**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
50:**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
53:**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
55:**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
58:**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
60:**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
62:**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
65:**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
67:**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
69:**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
71:**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
73:**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
75:**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
78:**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
80:**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
82:**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
84:**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the kind-count and volume-ratio release-notes lines over a fixture
# git repository and a fixture MODELINV log (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).

setup() {
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/tools/cycle-ratio.sh"
    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
    mkdir -p "$R"
    cd "$R"
    g() { git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null "$@"; }
    g init -q .
    printf 'echo 1\necho 2\n' > a.sh
    printf 'hello\nworld\n' > doc.md
    printf 'not counted\n' > notes.txt
    g add -A
    GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' g commit -q -m base
    FROM="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
    # a.sh: +3 -1; b.py: +2; c.ts: +1; doc.md: -"hello" +"hi there"; notes.txt and a binary not counted
    printf 'echo 1\necho 3\necho 4\necho 5\n' > a.sh
    printf 'x = 1\ny = 2\n' > b.py
    printf 'export {}\n' > c.ts
    printf 'hi there\nworld\n' > doc.md
    printf 'more\nlines\n' >> notes.txt
    printf '\000\001\002' > blob.sh
    g add -A
    GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' g commit -q -m change
    TO="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
    mkdir -p grimoires/loa .run
    {
        printf '# Sprint Plan: fixture\n\n**Date:** 2026-10-14\n\n## Sprint 1: One\n\n'
        printf '### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC-1 not a task · kind: operator\n\n'
        printf '### Technical Tasks\n'
        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.1: a → **[G-1]** ⇐ none · kind: mechanical\n'
        printf -- '- [x] Task 1.2: b → **[G-1]** · kind:mechanical\n'
        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.3: c → **[G-1]** · kind: judgment\n'
        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.4: d → **[G-1]** · kind: operator\n'
        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.5: untagged → **[G-1]**\n'
        printf '```\n- [ ] Task 9.9: fenced · kind: mechanical\n```\n\n'
        printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Two\n\n### Task 2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation\n'
        printf -- '- [ ] Task 2.E2E: validate → **[G-1]** · kind: judgment\n\n'
        printf '**Acceptance Criteria:**\n- [ ] Each goal validated · kind: mechanical\n\n'
        printf '## Appendix\n\n- [ ] Task 3.1: outside a sprint · kind: mechanical\n'
    } > grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    {
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-09-30T23:59:59.500000Z"}'
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-01T12:00:00.123456Z"}'
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-02T00:00:00Z"}'
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-02T00:00:01Z"}'
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"OTHER","ts_utc":"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z"}'
        printf '%s\n' 'not json at all'
        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"garbage"}'
    } > .run/model-invoke.jsonl
}

@test "CR-1 prints both lines with the counts, the mapping and the provenance" {
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    [[ "$output" == *"kinds: mechanical 2 · judgment 2 · operator 1"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"volume: script lines changed 7 (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed 15 (*.md) · model calls 2 (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: ${R}/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"* ]]
    # the untagged task line is named on stderr (bats merges it into output)
    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: 1 task line(s)"*"carry no kind: tag"* ]]
}

@test "CR-2 --json carries the same figures, the window and the untagged count" {
    run bash -c '"$0" --from "$1" --to "$2" --json 2>/dev/null' "$SCRIPT" "$FROM" "$TO"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '.kinds.mechanical' <<< "$output")" = 2 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.kinds.judgment' <<< "$output")" = 2 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.kinds.operator' <<< "$output")" = 1 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.kinds.untagged' <<< "$output")" = 1 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.volume.script_lines_changed' <<< "$output")" = 7 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.volume.prose_bytes_changed' <<< "$output")" = 15 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.volume.model_calls' <<< "$output")" = 2 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.volume.scope' <<< "$output")" = host ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.window.from' <<< "$output")" = "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.window.to' <<< "$output")" = "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.from' <<< "$output")" = "$FROM" ]
}

@test "CR-3 a missing MODELINV log yields model calls n/a and a WARN, exit 0" {
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO" --modelinv "$R/.run/absent.jsonl"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    [[ "$output" == *"model calls n/a (MODELINV rows"* ]]
    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: MODELINV log not found at $R/.run/absent.jsonl"* ]]
    run bash -c '"$0" --from "$1" --to "$2" --modelinv /nonexistent --json 2>/dev/null' "$SCRIPT" "$FROM" "$TO"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.volume.model_calls' <<< "$output")" = null ]
}

@test "CR-4 an unknown SHA exits 3; a SHA shaped like a flag exits 3" {
    run "$SCRIPT" --from 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --to "$TO"
    [ "$status" -eq 3 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"unknown commit"* ]]
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to --output=/tmp/x
    [ "$status" -eq 3 ]
}

@test "CR-5 usage errors exit 2: a missing --to, an unknown flag, an unreadable plan, outside a repo" {
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO" --bogus
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO" --sprint-plan "$R/nope.md"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    mkdir -p "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/norepo"
    cd "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/norepo"
    run env GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}" "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO"
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
}
